scored.title: Functional MRI parametric map-based radiomics nomograms for preoperative risk stratification of early-stage endometrial cancer: A multicenter study.
scored.why: This multicenter study of 362 patients built nomograms combining clinical factors, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), and radiomics features from functional MRI to predict deep myometrial invasion, tumor grade, and lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) in early endometrial cancer, with external test area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.785 to 0.906. The external validation and multicenter design are strengths, though radiomics-nomogram studies of this type are common and clinical impact on management decisions remains unproven.

scored.title: Clinical Implementation and Validation of Automated Slice-to-Volume Reconstruction for Fetal MRI Using a Vendor-Neutral MONAI-Based Imaging Informatics Pipeline.
scored.why: This single-center retrospective implementation study evaluated an automated MONAI-based pipeline for slice-to-volume reconstruction (SVR) of fetal MRI, reporting radiologist-rated acceptable reconstructions in 88-91% of 65 examinations with excellent inter-reader reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC, 0.92-0.93) and practical processing times. It demonstrates operational feasibility of an open-source pipeline in routine PACS workflow but lacks multi-vendor testing, diagnostic accuracy comparison, or outcome data, as the authors themselves note.

scored.title: Development of a prediction model for recurrence in patients with malignant ovarian germ cell tumors undergoing fertility-sparing surgery: A multicenter retrospective study.
scored.why: This multicenter retrospective study (n=264 across four hospitals in China) developed a Cox proportional hazards machine learning model to predict recurrence after fertility-sparing surgery for malignant ovarian germ cell tumors, achieving area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.838 and 0.851 for 3- and 5-year disease-free survival. Validation was limited to internal bootstrapping rather than an independent external cohort, so the model's real-world reliability is still uncertain.

scored.title: Precision or Paradox? AI-Driven Adiposity Imaging in Women With Overweight and Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
scored.why: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 38 studies (12,815 women) found that artificial intelligence (AI)-based segmentation of adiposity on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) was fast and accurate at the individual level, but pooled volumetric estimates showed extreme between-study heterogeneity (I² up to 100%), driven mostly by technical rather than biological factors. The key takeaway for the reader is a cautionary one: AI segmentation tools are not yet standardized enough across imaging protocols to support pooled or cross-study clinical use in women's obesity research.

scored.title: Supporting patient understanding of cervical and ovarian cancer: how well does AI perform?
scored.why: Five chatbots (ChatGPT 3.5, Gemini 2.0, Reddit Answers, Bootcamp, DeepSeek) answered standardized cervical and ovarian cancer frequently asked questions (FAQs), scored blinded by three gynecologic oncologists on a 4-point accuracy scale, with most models rated accurate but reading levels above 11th grade. This is a rubric-based accuracy and readability comparison without a clinician-answer comparator, making it routine for this beat despite its relevance to reproductive oncology.

scored.title: Machine learning-based prediction model for adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus.
scored.why: This study developed and validated (n=305 discovery, n=911 validation) machine learning models, including RandomForest and ExtraTree, to predict adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), achieving modest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values ranging from 0.616 to 0.726. The use of an independent validation cohort strengthens the design, but the modest discrimination limits immediate clinical utility as a decision support tool.

scored.title: Endometrial metabolomic profiling reveals disruption of fatty-acid metabolism in unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss.
scored.why: This prospective observational study used targeted quantitative metabolomics (630 metabolites via liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry) and machine learning to compare plasma and endometrial profiles across 80 women with recurrent implantation failure (RIF), unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss (U-RPL), and fertile controls, finding a 16-metabolite endometrial signature dominated by fatty-acid pathway disruption in U-RPL. The machine learning component is used mainly for signature discovery rather than as a clinical prediction tool, and the sample size is modest for biomarker discovery.

scored.title: Deep Learning Analysis of Prenatal Ultrasound for Identification of Ventriculomegaly.
scored.why: This study fine-tuned a vision transformer-based ultrasound foundation model (USF-MAE), pre-trained on over 370,000 images, for binary classification of fetal ventriculomegaly, achieving an F-score of about 91.8% on both cross-validation and an independent test cohort, outperforming standard baselines like ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16. The use of a large domain-specific pretrained foundation model with external test validation is methodologically notable, though the clinical task is narrow (single binary diagnosis) and real-world deployment data are absent.

scored.title: Evaluating a Guideline-Integrated Clinical Interaction Framework Vs a Standard Large Language Model Interaction for Dietary Recommendations in Recurrent Urolithiasis: In Silico Study.
scored.why: An in silico (computer-simulated) study compared a guideline-integrated large language model (LLM) framework (StoneAgent) against a standard LLM on 30 synthetic urolithiasis vignettes, finding higher Likert-scale scores for metabolic specificity, guideline adherence, and actionability, plus a nonsignificant safety advantage (100% vs 83.3% pass rate). The design offers a useful contrast between a structured clinical-reasoning pipeline and vanilla LLM output, but it uses synthetic vignettes rather than real patient interactions, limiting real-world generalizability.

scored.title: The reliability-clarity paradox in vascular digital health: A nurse-led evaluation of ChatGPT-4's accuracy in diabetic foot ulcer management.
scored.why: A cross-sectional evaluation had six wound-care nurses rate ChatGPT-4 responses on diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) management, finding near-perfect linguistic clarity (152/155) but poor scientific accuracy (6.67/10) against 2023 International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF) guidelines, with high inter-rater agreement measured by the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC=0.937)."The reliability-clarity paradox" is a useful framing of a real failure mode, but this is a single-center, single-model study without comparison to actual clinician answers.

scored.title: Supporting patient understanding of cervical and ovarian cancer: how well does AI perform?
scored.why: Five chatbots (ChatGPT 3.5, Gemini 2.0, Reddit Answers, Bootcamp, DeepSeek) answered standardized cervical and ovarian cancer frequently asked questions (FAQs), scored blinded by three gynecologic oncologists on a 4-point accuracy scale, with most models rated accurate but reading levels above 11th grade. This is a rubric-based accuracy and readability comparison without a clinician-answer comparator, making it routine for this beat despite its relevance to reproductive oncology.

scored.title: Large Language Model Responses to Common Otolaryngological Questions: Evaluating Accuracy, Appropriateness, Readability, and Hallucinations.
scored.why: ChatGPT-4.0 and Claude answered 36 otolaryngology patient questions, rated by two otolaryngologists for accuracy and readability using the Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) score, and both models hallucinated at least half of their cited references. The reference hallucination rate is a concrete, clinically relevant failure mode worth flagging, though the study lacks a clinician-answer comparator and uses a small question set.

scored.title: The Impact of Specific Prompt Engineering Techniques on the Readability of LLM-Generated Patient Materials in Gastroenterology and Hepatology.
scored.why: Researchers tested five prompt engineering techniques across twelve large language models (LLMs), measuring output readability with the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG) index and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) across 2,655 generated patient materials for gastroenterology topics; more constrained prompts improved readability but none reliably hit the target 6th grade level. The study is systematic in scope but stays within text-metric benchmarking with no clinician comparison or patient testing, so it is incremental for this beat.

scored.title: A five-phase evaluation framework for diagnostic and predictive medical artificial intelligence.
scored.why: This paper proposes a conceptual five-phase evaluation framework for medical artificial intelligence (AI), from technical validation through real-world integration, with phase-gating and fallback triggers for drift or safety signals, but presents no new data or validated application. It is a useful organizing scheme for thinking about AI maturity but offers no empirical finding that would change practice this week.

scored.title: Creating bottom-up RNA transfer vehicles from synthetic protein assemblies.
scored.why: This Nature paper uses generative AI-designed protein assemblies to build synthetic RNA delivery vehicles that outperform standard viral vectors in RNA transfer efficiency and demonstrates in vivo biodistribution and a gene-editing application in patient-derived cells and pigs. It is impressive protein engineering with an AI design component, but it is preclinical bioengineering rather than a clinical AI or patient-facing study, so it sits at the edge of these beats.

scored.title: Analysis of endometrial histopathological classifications and associated factors in infertile women with heterogeneous endometrial echogenicity.
scored.why: This retrospective cross-sectional study of 312 infertile women with heterogeneous endometrial echogenicity used logistic regression and an exploratory neural network to identify endometrial lesion risk factors, but the internally validated model achieved only modest discrimination (AUC 0.701) with no external validation. The modest performance and lack of external testing limit its practical utility for clinical decision-making.

scored.title: Comparative evaluation of large language models for text-based diagnostic reasoning in fetal central nervous system MRI: A retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study.
scored.why: A retrospective single-center study fed text summaries (no images) of 85 fetal central nervous system MRI cases to three large language models (LLMs), finding DeepSeek had the highest principal diagnosis match rate (77.6%) versus Gemini (69.4%) and ChatGPT (61.2%), though pairwise differences did not survive multiple-comparison correction. This is a text-only, image-stripped diagnostic reasoning task compared across models rather than against clinicians, so it offers little beyond confirming model variability on a narrow, artificial task.

scored.title: Stage-specific lipidomic signatures as biomarkers in progression of cervical cancer.
scored.why: This study used mass spectrometry lipidomics with machine learning to build a biomarker panel achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of about 0.945-0.946 for cervical cancer staging in a single-center Indian cohort. It has no external validation and the machine learning role is minimal, functioning mainly as a classifier atop biochemical assay data rather than a clinically deployable AI tool.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Implementation in Maternal and Child Health: A Scoping Review.
scored.why: This scoping review of artificial intelligence (AI) implementation in maternal and child health identified only seven studies meeting real-world implementation criteria out of 191 records screened, concluding evidence remains preliminary and heterogeneous. It offers no new data but is useful as a landscape summary showing how little real deployment evidence exists in this space.

scored.title: Quantitative morphometry of the cervix using deep learning and geometric area estimation techniques.
scored.why: This single-center study trained a YOLOv8 segmentation model plus geometric methods to estimate percentage of cervix visualized during colposcopy in 110 patients, with a hybrid method reaching a moderate Pearson correlation (r=0.72) against expert gynecologist ratings. The correlation is modest, the sample is small, and there is no external validation or clinical outcome tested.

scored.title: A deep learning method for preterm birth prediction using wavelet representations and auxiliary features from electrohysterogram.
scored.why: Researchers developed CWT-AuxNet, a deep learning model using continuous wavelet transform (CWT) representations of electrohysterogram (EHG) signals to predict preterm birth, reporting an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.741 at the window level and 0.932 at the user level. The study appears to be a methods development paper without mention of external validation or a comparison against established clinical predictors, limiting its immediate clinical relevance.

scored.title: Transient Elevation and Subsequent Normalization of Brain Age Gap During the Postpartum Period.
scored.why: This small longitudinal study (25 postpartum women, 30 nulliparous controls) used machine learning-based brain age prediction from MRI to find a transient elevation in brain age gap at 3 months postpartum that normalized by 12 months, with modest effect sizes and a between-group longitudinal difference that did not reach statistical significance. The sample size is small and the AI component is a supporting measurement tool rather than the study's main contribution, limiting generalizability despite an interesting biological hypothesis.

scored.title: Bump2Baby & Me+ (B2B&Me+): Protocol for a multi-country, European hybrid type 3 implementation-effectiveness study to reduce the incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus and improve maternal and child health.
scored.why: This is a study protocol for a multi-country hybrid type 3 implementation-effectiveness trial of a mobile health (mHealth) coaching intervention to reduce gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), using a machine learning screening tool (Monash machine learning GDM screening tool, MMLGDST) only as an entry criterion rather than as the object of evaluation. As a protocol paper, it describes planned methods rather than results, so its value to this reader is limited until outcome data are published.

scored.title: Multitask learning for ultrasound image classification and segmentation of endometrium in the diagnosis of ectopic pregnancy.
scored.why: This single-center study developed a multitask deep learning model to jointly classify and segment endometrium on transvaginal ultrasound images for distinguishing ectopic pregnancy from other early pregnancy conditions, achieving a modest area under the curve (AUC) of 0.85 for classification and a Dice coefficient of 0.81 for segmentation. The performance is moderate and there is no external validation or prospective clinical testing, limiting its immediate impact despite addressing a clinically important early diagnostic challenge.

scored.title: 'Healthy menopause': The European Menopause and Andropause Society (EMAS) 2026 framework for precision, digital, and interdisciplinary midlife health.
scored.why: This is a consensus position statement from the European Menopause and Andropause Society (EMAS) outlining a policy and care-delivery framework for menopause management that references digital tools and artificial intelligence (AI) governance but presents no primary data or evaluation. It is useful for situational awareness of policy direction but contains no algorithmic performance or clinical outcome to assess.

scored.title: V(2)-Former: Towards volumetric framework for instance-level segmentation and prediction of fetal ventriculomegaly in anisotropic MRI.
scored.why: This paper introduces V-Former, a transformer-based volumetric segmentation model for fetal ventriculomegaly on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), evaluated on a single retrospective dataset of 384 scans without external validation. The architecture is described as clinically motivated, but the lack of prospective or multi-site validation limits its translational relevance.

scored.title: Integration of inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers with machine learning enhances prediction of progesterone response in fertility-preserving endometrial carcinoma management.
scored.why: This retrospective single-center study (n=329) combined inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers with LASSO regression and machine learning to predict complete response to progesterone therapy in fertility-sparing endometrial carcinoma management, reporting area under the curve (AUC) values up to 0.933 in an internal validation cohort. The design lacks external multicenter validation, so generalizability of the nomogram remains unproven despite the strong internal discrimination.

scored.title: Machine learning-assisted SERS for rapid and accurate early screening of cervical cancer.
scored.why: This study built a machine learning classifier combining surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) serum spectra with principal component analysis and a multiple kernel support vector machine to screen for cervical cancer, reporting 97.1% classification accuracy in what appears to be a single-site retrospective dataset. No external validation or multicenter cohort is described, limiting confidence that this accuracy would generalize.

scored.title: E-InfertilityTest: Implementing an explainable AI framework for male infertility assessment.
scored.why: The authors built an explainable machine learning classifier from transcriptomic meta-analysis to distinguish fertile from infertile sperm samples in asthenozoospermia and teratozoospermia, releasing it as a standalone tool without prospective or external clinical validation. This is a proof-of-concept bioinformatics exercise rather than a clinically evaluated diagnostic, so its near-term relevance to practice is limited.

scored.title: A Coarse-to-Fine DoubleUNet Framework with Synergistic Loss for Accurate Fetal Head Circumference Measurement.
scored.why: This study proposes SDUNet, a coarse-to-fine deep learning segmentation framework with a novel synergistic loss function for automated fetal head circumference measurement from ultrasound, achieving a Dice coefficient of 98.60% and validating on an external dataset. The results are technically strong but represent an incremental architectural improvement on a well-studied benchmark task (HC18) without new clinical outcome data.

scored.title: SLC6A8-centered placental molecular signature predicts fetal growth restriction via machine learning and single-cell analysis.
scored.why: Using machine learning on placental gene expression datasets, this study identified a five-gene signature (including SLC6A8) predicting fetal growth restriction (FGR) and validated it across multiple retrospective datasets, further linking SLC6A8 to abnormal decidualization via single-cell analysis. The machine learning is used for biomarker discovery rather than as a deployable clinical prediction tool, and validation remains dataset-based rather than prospective.

scored.title: Predictive models for estimating the duration of labour induction: A systematic review and critical appraisal.
scored.why: This systematic review evaluated nine prediction models for labor induction duration, finding logistic regression as the dominant method with reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values from 0.73-0.88, but judged all models at high or unclear risk of bias by the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST) due to lack of external validation and calibration reporting. It is a useful synthesis showing the field's methodological immaturity rather than a new finding, so it mainly confirms that no model is yet ready for clinical use.

scored.title: Prediction of low birth weight using machine learning-based analysis of environmental and maternal risk factors: insights from the Korean CHildren's ENvironmental health study (Ko-CHENS).
scored.why: Using data from the Korean CHildren's ENvironmental health Study (Ko-CHENS) cohort of 4,893 mother-infant pairs, this study applied nine machine learning models to predict low birth weight (LBW) from 47 maternal and environmental variables, with random forest achieving the best area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AU-ROC) of 0.94, and identified trimester-specific air pollution associations. The very high AU-ROC without external validation raises concerns about overfitting or data leakage (e.g., gestational age as top predictor), limiting confidence in generalizability.

scored.title: Automatic detection of uterine contractions before and during labor using EHG: A systematic review.
scored.why: This systematic review of 50 studies compared thresholding, machine learning, and deep learning methods for detecting uterine contractions from electrohysterography (EHG) signals to monitor labor progression and preterm birth risk, using the QUADAS-2 tool to assess study quality. The review finds promising performance for adaptive thresholding methods but notes deep learning approaches are limited by small annotated datasets and inconsistent validation, so it is a useful field survey rather than a new clinical result.

scored.title: Comparative evaluation of large language models for text-based diagnostic reasoning in fetal central nervous system MRI: A retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study.
scored.why: A retrospective single-center study fed text summaries (no images) of 85 fetal central nervous system MRI cases to three large language models (LLMs), finding DeepSeek had the highest principal diagnosis match rate (77.6%) versus Gemini (69.4%) and ChatGPT (61.2%), though pairwise differences did not survive multiple-comparison correction. This is a text-only, image-stripped diagnostic reasoning task compared across models rather than against clinicians, so it offers little beyond confirming model variability on a narrow, artificial task.

scored.title: A comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-assisted and traditional methods of teaching diagnostic assessments to medical students: A randomized controlled study.
scored.why: A randomized controlled trial (RCT) of 80 medical students found that ChatGPT-assisted instruction improved theoretical exam scores and several Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX) domains compared to traditional teaching. This is an education intervention study rather than a patient-facing communication study, and the outcomes are proxy measures (test scores, student satisfaction) rather than real clinical impact or a direct comparison of AI against clinician performance with patients.

scored.title: Patient questions and artificial intelligence answers: Evaluating chatbots in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease.
scored.why: Eleven specialists rated responses from three chatbots (ChatGPT 5.1, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5) to 12 patient questions about aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD), finding Gemini scored highest for accuracy but all models produced text at a postgraduate reading level. This is a routine rubric-based evaluation with expert raters but no comparison to actual clinician answers or patient outcomes, so it adds little beyond confirming the now-familiar finding that chatbot text is too complex for patients.

scored.title: Guideline-Based Evaluation of Five Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Platforms for Clinician-Oriented Questions on Open Temporomandibular Joint Surgery.
scored.why: Two blinded oral and maxillofacial surgeons rated responses from five generative AI chatbots to 40 clinician-oriented questions on open temporomandibular joint (TMJ) surgery using quality and readability tools, finding no single platform dominated all metrics and inter-rater reliability was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) 0.93-0.99). This is another rubric-based, clinician-facing chatbot comparison without a direct human-clinician answer comparator, placing it in the routine tier for this beat.

scored.title: Performance of large language models as a source of clinical information on bacteriophage therapy.
scored.why: Twelve clinicians and researchers rated large language model (LLM) responses to 20 patient questions about bacteriophage therapy across accuracy, completeness, clarity, and tone/empathy, finding generally favorable but modestly variable scores (adjusted means 3.36-3.96 of 5) and wrong information in 20% of responses. This is a routine expert-rubric evaluation without a clinician-answer comparator, though the notable error rate on an emerging, poorly standardized therapy area is a modest point of interest.

scored.title: Will They Use It? Patient and Provider Acceptance of Chatbot Screening and Counseling for Hereditary Cancer Syndromes in a Geographically Underserved Population.
scored.why: A survey of 66 primary care providers and 476 residents in rural Southwest Virginia found substantial interest in chatbot-assisted hereditary cancer syndrome screening and counseling, with about 77% of providers and 82% of residents viewing it favorably. This is an acceptability survey with no actual chatbot deployment or performance data, limiting its evidentiary weight despite documenting a real access gap.

scored.title: Bridging the Health Literacy Gap for Patients With Oral Cancer: Readability Enhancement With AI Chatbots.
scored.why: Three large language models (LLMs) simplified NHS oral cancer patient education materials, improving readability scores significantly (p<0.0001) while maintaining semantic similarity to source text measured by latent semantic analysis (LSA), with Claude achieving the target Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES) of 80. This is a readability-improvement demonstration without clinician comparison or patient outcome data, a routine finding for this beat.

scored.title: Evaluating the quality of artificial intelligence responses to psoriasis-related clinical and patient questions: a comparative study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot.
scored.why: Three chatbots (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) answered 54 psoriasis-related diagnostic, treatment, and patient questions, scored by three dermatologists on an 8-point accuracy and safety scale, with Gemini scoring highest overall (7.77) and highest reliability rate (92.6%). This is a rubric-based chatbot comparison without a clinician-answer benchmark, a routine design for this beat despite substantial rater agreement.

scored.title: Using an educator-guided generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tool for developing communication skills in undergraduate pharmacy students.
scored.why: A quasi-experimental study of an educator-guided generative AI (GenAI) simulation tool, ATLAS, found pharmacy students who used it before Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) improved communication scores significantly (median increase 1.55 points, p=0.0045) versus no change in non-users. This measures an actual skill outcome with a comparison group, though it concerns training future clinicians rather than direct patient-facing communication, and lacks randomization to rule out self-selection bias.

scored.title: Quality and safety of large language model generated communication in psychodermatology: a bilingual scenario-based evaluation.
scored.why: Five large language models (LLMs) responded to 16 bilingual psychodermatology scenarios, rated by three blinded clinicians across communication domains, with Gemini 2.5 Flash scoring highest and all models showing weaker actionability and risk management than empathy. This is a rubric-based multi-model comparison without a clinician-generated comparator, a routine design though the language-based performance gap (Turkish versus English) is a modestly useful finding.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence in Patient Education: ChatGPT for Penile Prosthesis Surgery Counseling, a Likert Scale Analysis.
scored.why: A panel of seven urologists rated ChatGPT (GPT-4) responses to 15 patient FAQs about penile prosthesis surgery on a four-point Likert scale, finding acceptable but not high scores for accuracy and misinformation risk. This is a rubric-based evaluation with no comparison to actual clinician answers or patient outcomes, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Can AI chatbots guide patients and physicians about neck pain? A reliability and readability comparison of ChatGPT-4 and Gemini.
scored.why: ChatGPT-4 and Gemini were compared on 24 patient questions and 4 case scenarios about neck pain using validated tools including modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) for reliability and Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) for readability; Gemini scored higher on reliability but both were rated difficult to read, and clinical accuracy in case scenarios was similar between models. This is a head-to-head chatbot comparison without a clinician baseline, placing it in the routine tier for this beat.

scored.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Align with Evidence? Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Knee Osteoarthritis Surgical Guidelines.
scored.why: ChatGPT-4o's answers to 20 clinical practice guideline (CPG) recommendations for knee osteoarthritis surgery were classified by two reviewers, showing 60% concordance with guidelines (Cohen's kappa 0.392) and poor consistency across repeated queries. This measures guideline adherence rather than patient communication quality against a clinician benchmark, and the low reproducibility across repeated sessions is a notable limitation.

scored.title: Cross specialty evaluation of large language model responses on intentional replantation.
scored.why: ChatGPT 4.0 and OpenEvidence were compared on 20 questions about intentional tooth replantation, with endodontists and oral-maxillofacial surgeons rating accuracy and completeness via linear mixed-effects models; OpenEvidence scored significantly higher on both measures. The cross-specialty comparison is somewhat novel, but this remains a rubric-based chatbot-versus-chatbot comparison without a clinician-generated answer as the benchmark.

scored.title: Applying Artificial Intelligence to Facial Feminization Surgery: Understanding of Facial Anatomy, Surgical Techniques, and Patient Education.
scored.why: ChatGPT and Google Bard were queried on 9 questions about facial feminization surgery and rated blindly by five expert reviewers using modified AI-DISCERN criteria at baseline and 3 months later; ChatGPT initially outperformed Bard but Bard improved over time. This is a small, rubric-based comparison without a clinician benchmark or patient outcome measure, typical for this beat's routine tier.

scored.title: Digital pathology, image analysis, and artificial intelligence in liver disease.
scored.why: This is a narrative review summarizing advances in digital pathology, whole-slide image analysis, and deep learning applied to liver disease diagnosis and transplant assessment, without presenting new data or a validated model. It restates known applications and challenges rather than offering a finding that would change clinical practice.

scored.title: Large Language Models and Adverse Event Detection Within Immunotherapy Clinical Trials.
scored.why: The title indicates a study of large language models (LLMs) for detecting adverse events within immunotherapy clinical trials, but no abstract text was provided to assess methods, comparator, or findings. Without data on design or effect size this cannot be scored on its merits and is treated conservatively.

scored.title: Ethics and Professionalism in Artificial Intelligence and Medical Practice: A Position Paper From the American College of Physicians.
scored.why: This American College of Physicians position paper offers ethical guidance on artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical practice, articulating principles like relationality, self-governance, and competence, but contains no new empirical data or study design. It is commentary intended to shape professional norms rather than a finding that would change clinical action.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence in assisted localization of fetal ultrasound standard planes: a narrative review.
scored.why: This is a narrative review summarizing existing literature on artificial intelligence (AI) methods for automated localization of fetal ultrasound standard planes, without presenting new experimental data or validation. It surveys known techniques like convolutional neural networks and reinforcement learning but offers no new finding.

scored.title: Predicting Insecticide-Treated Net Use Among Under-Five Children in Tanzania Using Machine Learning: Evidence From the 2022 Tanzania DHS.
scored.why: This study applied several supervised machine learning models to predict insecticide-treated bed net use among children under five in Tanzania using national survey data, with Random Forest achieving the best performance (AUC 0.90). The topic concerns malaria prevention behavior rather than reproductive or obstetric health, and it has no meaningful connection to the reproductive medicine or clinical AI beats this reader follows.

scored.title: Patient and parent voices in tetralogy of Fallot: A French social media analysis.
scored.why: This retrospective observational study used natural language processing and sentiment analysis on 1,291 French-language social media posts to characterize the concerns of patients and parents affected by tetralogy of Fallot, a congenital heart defect. While methodologically reasonable, the topic sits outside reproductive and obstetric health and does not involve substantial clinical AI evaluation, limiting its relevance to this reader's beats.

scored.title: Explainable ensemble machine learning for pregnancy screening in dairy cows using routine dairy herd improvement records.
scored.why: This retrospective study built an ensemble machine learning model, combining random forest, XGBoost, and logistic regression, to screen pregnancy status in dairy cows using routine Dairy Herd Improvement (DHI) test-day records, achieving an AUC of 0.857 with cross-farm generalization. Despite the word 'pregnancy' in the title, this is veterinary agricultural science with no connection to human reproductive or obstetric medicine.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Radiology Gap-Filler in Somalia: A Narrative Review with a Pragmatic Implementation Framework.
scored.why: This is a narrative review proposing a pragmatic framework for deploying artificial intelligence (AI) radiology tools like computer-aided tuberculosis screening in Somalia, without any original data, trial, or deployment reported. It is a policy and implementation commentary rather than an evaluation of a clinical AI system.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence for systemic therapy selection and prediction of outcomes in advanced gynecological cancers.
scored.why: This is a narrative review summarizing artificial intelligence (AI)-based biomarker approaches, including computational pathology and radiomics, for predicting therapy response in advanced gynecologic cancers, without presenting new data. The authors themselves note small sample sizes, limited discriminative power, and absence of prospective validation across the cited literature.

scored.title: Mapping ovarian cellular and molecular landscape across the lifespan of women: a scoping review.
scored.why: This scoping review maps multi-omic studies of the ovarian lifecycle from fetal development through menopause, identifying inconsistencies across transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic datasets, with artificial intelligence (AI) mentioned only as a future direction. No new experimental or algorithmic work is presented.

scored.title: Application of cell-free RNA in liquid biopsy.
scored.why: This review surveys cell-free RNA (cfRNA) liquid biopsy technology across oncology and pregnancy complication prediction, discussing artificial intelligence (AI) and multi-omics integration as future directions rather than reporting original results. It is a broad, largely non-quantitative synthesis with no new clinical evaluation.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence-augmented robotic surgery in gynecologic oncology: intraoperative assistance and analytics.
scored.why: This narrative review summarizes emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in robotic-assisted gynecologic oncology surgery, including computer vision for surgical phase recognition and predictive analytics, without presenting new experimental data. The authors themselves note that most applications remain in early validation stages, limiting the item's news value.

scored.title: Deep learning assisting the surgical management of gynecologic cancers.
scored.why: This narrative review discusses deep learning applications in gynecologic cancer surgery, including surgical skill assessment, intraoperative anatomical recognition, and outcome prediction, without presenting new data. The authors acknowledge that most underlying studies are retrospective, small, and lack external validation, so no substantive new evidence is offered.

scored.title: Prenatal exposure to residential greenness and artificial light at night and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children aged 4-12 years: A retrospective cohort study in China.
scored.why: This retrospective cohort study of 814 Chinese children examined associations between prenatal residential greenness, artificial light at night (ALAN), and neurodevelopmental outcomes using multivariable regression and some interpretable machine learning for exposure analysis, finding urban-specific associations with cognitive, motor, and autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related traits. The AI component is peripheral to an otherwise conventional environmental epidemiology study, and it falls outside the reproductive or clinical AI focus of this digest.

scored.title: Understanding the importance of social and environmental stressors in predicting maternal sleep quality during late pregnancy.
scored.why: Using gradient boosting machine learning on 687 pregnant women in the MADRES cohort, this study identified mental health, sociodemographic, and environmental exposures (noise, ozone, organophosphate esters) as top predictors of poor late-pregnancy sleep quality, achieving a modest test area under the curve (AUC) of 0.704. The predictive performance is weak and the study is exploratory feature-ranking rather than a validated clinical tool.

scored.title: Dnq-unet: a two-level fusion framework for few-shot domain adaptation in cervical cancer CTV segmentation.
scored.why: This paper introduces DNQ-UNet, a dual-encoder deep learning architecture combining spatially adaptive normalization (SPADE) and cross-attention for few-shot domain adaptation in cervical cancer clinical target volume (CTV) segmentation, showing improved Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) over baselines like nnU-Net V2 with as few as 5-10 fine-tuning cases. This is a purely technical radiotherapy contouring engineering advance with no patient outcome data and limited direct relevance to the reader's reproductive or clinical AI focus.

scored.title: Automated evidence surveillance with AI-enabled preranking with cutoff in living guideline maintenance: a simulation study.
scored.why: This simulation study evaluated automated evidence retrieval workflows, including artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled preranking with cutoff thresholds, for maintaining living clinical guidelines, using the 2023 International Polycystic Ovary Syndrome guidelines as a test case, finding overarching database searches outperformed topic-specific searches in recall and workload reduction. This is a methodological, meta-research contribution about literature surveillance infrastructure rather than a clinical AI application affecting patient care directly.

scored.title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.
scored.why: This cross-sectional survey of 419 diabetic patients in Saudi Arabia used structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine relationships between digital health engagement, trust in AI-based Ministry of Health (MOH) chatbot services, and information-seeking behavior, finding moderate trust with most patients viewing AI tools as supportive rather than decision-making. As a self-reported attitudinal survey without any direct evaluation of chatbot performance, clinician comparison, or patient outcomes, it offers limited actionable evidence for this reader's research area.

scored.title: An expert-based assessment of the quality, reliability, understandability, and readability of ChatGPT responses on cerebral palsy.
scored.why: An expert panel of 20 physiotherapists rated ChatGPT's answers to cerebral palsy questions using the DISCERN quality tool and Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT), finding average quality (DISCERN 45) and poor understandability/actionability, with all text above high-school reading level. This is another rubric-scored chatbot evaluation without a clinician-answer comparator, fitting the routine pattern the beat already expects.

scored.title: How Do GenAI Chatbots Communicate Fluoride Information? A Readability and Negative Framing Analysis.
scored.why: A cross-sectional study analyzed 1,326 sentences from five generative AI chatbots answering fluoride-related questions, finding 286 (22%) were negatively framed, more often in fact-checking prompts, with generally difficult readability despite improved structure. This is a content-analysis study without any comparison to clinician communication or measured patient impact, so it mainly documents a framing bias rather than a clinically actionable finding.

scored.title: What Platform Scores Miss: Multidimensional Evaluation of AI Teaching Agents in Medical Education.
scored.why: A study of eight AI teaching agents used in an endocrinology medical education curriculum found that platform-generated quality scores diverged substantially from an independently applied 8-dimension rubric, with agent rankings sometimes inverted between the two scoring methods. This is a medical education evaluation tool study rather than a patient-facing communication study, and its intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) of 0.51 for agreement with expert raters indicates only moderate reliability.

scored.title: Student Perceptions of Virtual Counseling Practice Using ChatGPT Voice Mode in Pharmacy Education.
scored.why: A post-intervention survey of 137 pharmacy students who used ChatGPT voice mode as a simulated patient found high satisfaction with accessibility and feedback but mixed views on realism, using descriptive statistics and item-objective congruence for questionnaire validity. This is a perception survey with no objective measure of counseling competency and no clinician comparator, making it a routine educational feasibility report rather than a finding about patient communication.

scored.title: Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models for Surgical Case Creation.
scored.why: Five large language models (LLMs) generated trauma surgery training case scenarios for a simulation platform, rated by four board-certified surgeons using a modified quality framework, with Claude-3.5-sonnet scoring highest. This concerns educational content generation for trainees rather than patient-facing communication, and is a routine benchmark comparison without patient or clinical outcome data.

scored.title: Development of a Conversational AI Intervention for Preventing Illegal Filming Among South Korean Adolescents: A Pediatric Health Perspective.
scored.why: Researchers developed a conversational artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot named "No Cam" to educate South Korean adolescents about illegal filming prevention, tested via focus interviews and a formative usability evaluation with only ten students. This is an early-stage feasibility and design study without a comparator, outcome measure, or scale needed to judge real effectiveness.

scored.title: Applications of artificial intelligence along the perioperative pathway in metabolic and bariatric surgery.
scored.why: This scoping review identified 58 studies on artificial intelligence (AI) across the perioperative pathway of metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS), noting most concerned postoperative outcome prediction and finding minimal external validation or prospective clinical evaluation across the field. As a broad narrative synthesis without new primary data, it offers limited actionable evidence beyond flagging the field's immaturity.

scored.title: Co-designing DESI-Heart: Conversational agent based self-care intervention for people with cardiovascular disease.
scored.why: This describes a participatory co-design process for a culturally tailored conversational agent (CA) for cardiovascular self-care among the Indian diaspora in Australia, involving workshops and thematic analysis rather than any AI system testing or evaluation. No chatbot was actually built, deployed, or compared against clinicians, so it offers little of substance for this beat's focus on measured AI performance.

scored.title: ChatGPT and other large language models for childhood asthma.
scored.why: This is a narrative review discussing large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini in childhood asthma care, summarizing existing evidence and potential risks like hallucinations and bias without presenting new data or comparisons. As a review with no original findings, it falls into the low-value tier for this beat.

scored.title: Annals On Call - Is Artificial Intelligence Eroding Clinical Competence?
scored.why: This is an opinion column titled 'Is Artificial Intelligence Eroding Clinical Competence?' with no abstract text provided, so no empirical claim can be assessed. It appears to be commentary rather than a study.

scored.title: Integrated multi-omics analyses identify an RAS-SLC11A2-associated molecular framework linking iron metabolism with PCOS-related cardiometabolic risk.
scored.why: This is a basic-science multi-omics study using transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and Mendelian randomization to link an iron-metabolism gene (SLC11A2) to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)-related cardiometabolic risk, with machine learning used only as an ancillary classification tool. There is no clinical AI application here, and the work is mechanistic and preclinical, testing a candidate drug in what appears to be cell or animal models rather than patients.

scored.title: Advanced detection of fetal arrhythmia utilizing spatial deep convolutional neural network with GHA-DenseNet for enhanced electrocardiographic signal processing.
scored.why: This paper proposes a novel deep learning architecture combining several named modules (Kalman filtering, SMOTE, wavelet-based feature extraction, DenseNet variant optimized by a bio-inspired algorithm) for fetal arrhythmia detection from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, reporting only relative F1-score improvements over unspecified baselines with no dataset details, clinical validation, or comparison against clinician diagnosis. It reads as an engineering benchmark paper with essentially no clinical grounding provided in the abstract.

scored.title: SemanticST: A Scalable Multi-Contextual Graph Learning Framework for Uncovering Spatial Niches and Robust Multi-Sample Integration in Spatial Transcriptomics.
scored.why: This paper presents SemanticST, a graph neural network (GNN) framework for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data, benchmarked on brain, embryo, and tumor tissue datasets including breast cancer samples. It is a general computational biology methods paper with no direct clinical application, patient outcome data, or reproductive health focus beyond incidental embryo tissue mentioned as one benchmark dataset.

scored.title: Vaginal drug delivery for precision therapy in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: emerging technologies, translational challenges and future perspectives.
scored.why: This is a narrative review discussing vaginal drug delivery technologies for a proposed condition termed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), with artificial intelligence and machine learning mentioned only briefly as one of several future directions among many. There is no original data, trial, or AI evaluation presented, making this an opinion and perspective piece rather than a research finding.

scored.title: Comparative genomics and reproductive mechanisms of fertility in cattle and camels: Implications for assisted reproduction and precision breeding.
scored.why: This narrative review synthesizes comparative genomics and reproductive physiology in cattle and camels for assisted reproductive technology (ART) and precision breeding, with artificial intelligence mentioned only as an emerging tool. It has no relevance to human reproductive medicine or clinical AI application.

scored.title: Augmenting Pediatric Care With Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Responsibilities for Nurse Practitioners.
scored.why: This is a narrative review discussing potential applications of artificial intelligence (AI) for nurse practitioners in pediatric and adolescent care, including a brief mention of reproductive health education, without presenting original data or evaluation. It offers no new evidence and only tangential reproductive relevance.

scored.title: Comparative evaluation of machine-learning algorithms for early detection of metritis in dairy cows.
scored.why: This is a veterinary study developing and externally validating machine learning models, including a stacking ensemble achieving 88.7% accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.94, to predict metritis in dairy cows using calving records. Despite solid methodology with external validation, the subject is animal agriculture and has no relevance to human reproductive or clinical medicine.

scored.title: DEHP-induced male reproductive toxicity: Evidence from population studies, animal experiments, and multi-omics profiling.
scored.why: This multi-level study combined National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) epidemiological data, rat experiments, and machine learning-based transcriptomic hub-gene identification to link di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure to testosterone deficiency and testicular toxicity, ultimately using computational docking to propose ursolic acid as a candidate therapeutic. The machine learning here is a minor bioinformatics tool within a toxicology study and does not constitute a clinically relevant AI application.

scored.title: TFRC-mediated immune exclusion as a therapeutic vulnerability in cervical cancer: A comprehensive analysis based on the cancer immunoediting process.
scored.why: This study used bioinformatic analysis and ensemble machine learning (LASSO, random forest, XGBoost) on public gene expression datasets to derive a four-gene prognostic signature for cervical cancer immune exclusion, centered on TFRC, and validated its oncogenic role through in vitro and xenograft experiments. The work is fundamentally a molecular oncology and immunology study with machine learning used only as a bioinformatic screening tool, offering little of direct relevance to clinical AI applications.

scored.title: Assumptions and principles for responsible AI development and use in grief and bereavement care.
scored.why: This is a conceptual and ethics paper proposing a taxonomy of "Grief AI" applications and risk categories for artificial intelligence in bereavement care, with no original data, evaluation, or clinical outcome reported. It is commentary rather than empirical research, placing it well below the bar for a research-focused digest.

scored.title: AI Use, Perceptions, and Perceived Impact Among Nursing Students: Cross-Sectional Study.
scored.why: This entry is an authors' reply in a journal correspondence exchange, with no abstract or original data provided in the text. Without any described methods or findings, it cannot be evaluated for clinical or research relevance.

scored.title: Who Reviews the Rewrite? Separating Patient-Initiated and Institutionally Curated Large Language Model Simplification.
scored.why: This entry is a commentary piece with no abstract or content text provided, addressing methodological questions about patient-initiated versus institutionally curated large language model (LLM) text simplification. Without any substantive text, its research value cannot be assessed.

scored.title: AI-driven health misinformation in Somalia's digital era: A neglected crisis demanding global action.
scored.why: This is a letter to the editor discussing the risk of AI-driven health misinformation in Somalia, with no original data, study design, or measured outcome. It is an opinion and advocacy piece rather than empirical research.

scored.title: [Use of artificial intelligence in clinical practice and hospitals].
scored.why: This is a narrative review discussing general applications of artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models in urology, covering documentation, imaging, and patient communication without presenting new data or a study design. It offers no findings, evaluation, or comparator and is purely commentary.

scored.title: PRACTALL 2025: Artificial intelligence-application of allergy and immunology to patient care.
scored.why: This is a position paper from the PRACTALL allergy-immunology collaboration describing the general landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare, including chatbots and ambient documentation, without presenting original data. It is commentary intended to orient allergist-immunologists to AI trends rather than a study with a measurable finding.

scored.title: Toward an AI-integrated nursing curriculum: A Kano model analysis of generative AI competency needs.
scored.why: A cross-sectional survey of 1219 clinical nurses in China used the Kano model to categorize generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) training needs, finding high prior usage (87.7%) but low formal training (7.4%). This concerns curriculum planning rather than patient-facing communication and contains no comparator or outcome measure relevant to this beat.

scored.title: Leveraging generative AI to enhance doctor-patient communication.
scored.why: No abstract text was provided for this piece on generative artificial intelligence (AI) and doctor-patient communication, so nothing can be assessed beyond the title suggesting a commentary or perspective article. Without data or study design, this cannot be scored as a substantive contribution to the field.

scored.title: MedCity FemFwd: How Midwives Can Support the Maternal Health Crisis
scored.why: This is a podcast episode interview with a certified nurse midwife (CNM) discussing physician-midwifery collaboration and maternal health, containing no concrete company action, product, funding, or regulatory event. It is thought leadership content with nothing that moved the industry this week.

scored.title: CORRIGENDUM: Impact of multimodal information on the estimation of fetal growth indicators using machine learning regression models (2026Biomed. Phys. Eng. Express 12 035005).
scored.why: This is a corrigendum notice for a prior article on fetal growth prediction with no substantive text or findings provided. There is nothing here to evaluate.

scored.title: High-resolution 3D micro-CT reveals an additional muscle layer in esophageal atresia.
scored.why: This study used micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) and basic machine learning image segmentation software to characterize esophageal muscle anatomy in esophageal atresia, a congenital malformation unrelated to reproductive or obstetric health beyond incidental fetal tissue samples. It has no clinical AI component of note and falls outside all three beats.

scored.title: Are global health commitments relevant in low-income countries? Considering discussions at Davos 2026.
scored.why: This is an opinion commentary discussing global health policy priorities from the 2026 World Economic Forum, touching on artificial intelligence (AI) and women's health only as broad conceptual themes without any study, data, or concrete finding. It contains no clinical AI evaluation, reproductive medicine research, or industry news of a specific action taken.

scored.title: Corrigendum to 'Intrapartum electronic fetal heart rate monitoring to predict acidemia at birth with the use of deep learning' [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology 232/1 (2025) 116-117].
scored.why: This is a corrigendum notice for a prior deep learning study on intrapartum electronic fetal heart rate monitoring, with no substantive content provided. There is nothing here to evaluate for clinical or methodological significance.

scored.title: Correction to "Machine learning versus traditional formulas for fetal weight estimation: An international multicenter study evaluating prediction accuracy across birth weight percentiles".
scored.why: This is a bibliographic correction notice with no substantive scientific content included in the text. There is nothing here for the reader to evaluate.

scored.title: Reply : Enhancing patient education in cataract surgery using a conversational artificial intelligence chatbot: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
scored.why: This is an author reply to a letter regarding a prior randomized controlled trial (RCT) on chatbot-based cataract surgery education, with no abstract or new data provided. There is nothing substantive here to evaluate.

scored.title: Comment on: Enhancing patient education in cataract surgery using a conversational artificial intelligence chatbot: pilot randomized controlled trial.
scored.why: This is a letter commenting on a prior randomized controlled trial (RCT) of a chatbot for cataract surgery patient education, with no text or data provided. There is no content to assess.
